From 2026-09-09 ~16:28Z to at least 18:17Z digicoll.lib.berkeley.edu answered EVERY request under /record/* and /search* with HTTP 202 + header 'x-amzn-waf-action: challenge' and a zero-length body (an AWS WAF JavaScript challenge). Confirmed with curl over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, with the audit UA, a Chrome UA and no UA, with HEAD, plain GET and Range GET, and with python urllib; and by four separate polling runs totalling ~25 minutes of 30-second retries (17:31-17:36Z, 17:53-17:58Z, 18:04-18:09Z, 18:10-18:17Z). Never once did the body begin with %PDF. SCOPE OF THE BLOCK, MEASURED: only /record/* and /search* are challenged. Still open and used here: https://digicoll.lib.berkeley.edu/oai2d (OAI-PMH, verb=GetRecord&metadataPrefix=marcxml - the Bancroft's own catalogue record for the same item), digicoll /robots.txt, content.cdlib.org (the associated diseno maps), www.oac.cdlib.org (the collection finding aid) and calisphere.org. So the item metadata is reachable and only the page images are not. ROUTES TRIED AND DEAD: Merritt via the ark in MARC 951$a redirects into an endless guest_login loop (merritt.cdlib.org/m/ark%3A%2F13030%2F... -> /guest_login -> /home/choose_collection -> ...); the Wayback Machine has no capture of these PDFs; archive.org holds exactly one cubanc_lcf item (Ballona, SD) and it is not one of these; Calisphere returns 404 for the Merritt arks. I did NOT attempt to solve, replay or evade the WAF challenge. RETRY ADVICE: poll the PDF URL directly, not the record page, and treat anything that is not %PDF in the first four bytes as a failure - the challenge returns HTTP 202, a SUCCESS code, so any checker that tests the status code alone will record a false success and write a zero-byte file (/tmp/casefile-cache already holds two such zero-byte files, cubanc_lcf_sd157.pdf and cubanc_lcf_nd324.pdf, left by other agents in this same pass). || EVIDENCE TIER: MARC/OAI catalogue record, NOT a PDF page. Per method, year/governor/grantee/outcome must be graded against the concession decree or its sworn translation inside the case file, so those stay UV. name and land_case are graded from the Bancroft's own item-level catalogue (024$a docket, 035$a and 856$u filename, 245$a caption), which is the same authority the red label carries; evidence strings therefore cite MARC fields instead of a stamped page, which is a deviation from the output contract and is flagged here. || RECORD 5 OF 6. SD 122 AND SD 128 ARE THE SAME LAND AND MUST BE GRADED TOGETHER. Bowman (MARC 520$a on both records) describes one grant made twice: '(1) Apl. 15, 1837, to Ignacio Palomares and Ricardo Vijar, about 1.5 leagues, by name, and (2) Mar. 14, 1840, to Ricardo Vijar, Ignacio Palomares and Luis Arenas, the above grant and an augmentation of 1 league to San Jose. On Feb. 12, 1846, the grant was partitioned among the three grantees.' So the TWO-name grantee set belongs to 1837 and the THREE-name set (with Arenas) belongs to 1840. Both dockets carry the identical Commission and District Court dates (Board 31 Jan 1854, District Court 25 Feb 1856, appeal dismissed 23 Feb 1857) and both were patented to the same trio, Dalton/Palomares/Vijar, on different days in 1875 under GLO 457 and 458. Original portfolio 122 p. (MARC 300$a); Spanish text pp. 11-19 and 31-58 (MARC 500$a) - two large Spanish blocks, consistent with both the 1837 concession and the 1840 regrant/partition papers being bound in. Associated numbers: Toma 58, Filed Expediente 75, Unclassified Expediente 124, Expediente 141, Docket 365, 122 SD, 121 SD, GLO 457 - Docket 365 matches hoffman_1862.commission_no 365. Seven associated diseno maps are listed in MARC 856 (B-1125 to B-1127, D-1124, D-1128, D-1129, E-1130) and those are on content.cdlib.org, a different host from the blocked one. Register patent columns (Henry Dalton, Ignacio Palomares, and Ricardo Vijar / Dec. 4, 1875 / GLO 457 / 4,430.64 acres) match MARC 520$a exactly.

name.evidence: MARC 245$a (OAI rec. 265868): 'San Jose [Los Angeles County] Ricardo Vejar and Ignacio Palomares, Claimants. Case no. 128, Southern District of California.' The register's 'San Jose Addition' is not the Bancroft caption but it is substantively right and it does the disambiguating work SD 122's label failed at: MARC 520$a describes this docket's grant as 'the above grant and an augmentation of 1 league to San Jose', i.e. the addition. NO PDF PAGE.

year.evidence: THE ONE HARD YEAR PROBLEM IN THIS CHUNK. The register pairs year 1837 with grantee 'R. Vejar, Ignacio Palomares and Luis Arenas'. Per MARC 520$a those two facts belong to different grants: '(1) Apl. 15, 1837, to Ricardo Vijar and Ignacio Palomares, about 1.5 leagues, by name, and (2) Mar. 14, 1840, to Ricardo Vijar, Ignacio Palomares and Luis Arenas, the above grant and an augmentation of 1 league'. Luis Arenas enters only in 1840, and the AUGMENTATION - which is what 'Addition' names - is the 1840 act. The correct year for the grant this row describes is 1840. Note the register could not have taken 1837 from a decree with Arenas in it, and Hoffman is no check here: hoffman_1862 prints year 1837 with governor AND grantee BLANK for court no. 128, so the register's three-name grantee string came from somewhere other than Hoffman while the year came from Hoffman - the conflation is mechanically explained. GRADED ERR ON CATALOGUE EVIDENCE, NOT ON A DECREE PAGE; the concession is in the Spanish block at pp. 8-19 (MARC 500$a) and a re-reader must confirm there.

Alvarado made both the 1837 grant and the 1840 regrant per MARC 520$a, so the register's 'Alvarado' survives the year problem either way; but hoffman_1862.governor is null for this docket and no decree was read, so this is not confirmed.

Vejar, Ignacio Palomares and Luis Arenas' matches the THREE grantees of the 1840 regrant in MARC 520$a. But MARC 700 for this record lists only TWO $e='Grantee' entries, Palomares and Vejar - Arenas is absent from the name-authority block though present in the 520 narrative, an internal inconsistency in the Bancroft record itself.
